items.title: Food bank network targets record-breaking Holiday Drive in Mississauga
items.summary: Food Banks Mississauga is setting its sights on raising a record amount of money as it launches its 2026 Holiday Drive in support of the growing number of families who struggle to put food on the table. 3 million for this year’s campaign. Food Banks Mississauga raised just over $3 million during its 2024 Holiday Drive. This year’s initiative, sponsored by Walmart Canada, kicked off on Monday and continues until Jan. 8, 2027. Food bank officials in Canada’s seventh-largest city said their latest drive “comes at a crucial time as one in 10 children in Mississauga relied on Food Banks Mississauga and its citywide network” of more than 60 food programs last year, as noted in the agency’s Annual Impact Report. The report, released late this past summer, “shows that the most vulnerable neighbours are turning to a food bank for support,” Food Banks Mississauga officials said in a news release on Tuesday. ” This past year, people in Mississauga visited food programs 513,000 times, the most ever in the organization’s 40-year history, according to FBM. “This record number of food bank visits remains 444 per cent higher than just 10 years ago and is now the new normal,” the agency said.

items.title: Job fair will connect newcomers to Canada with Mississauga employers
items.summary: Finding work is one of the biggest challenges facing many newcomers to Canada, particularly those trying to establish careers while navigating an unfamiliar job market. A free event coming to Mississauga hopes to make that process a little easier. The Canadian Immigrant Newcomer Fair will bring employers, educational institutions, career advisers and settlement organizations together at the Living Arts Centre on Friday, Nov. 13, offering newcomers and others looking for work an opportunity to make connections and explore their options. The event comes at a time when Canada’s job market is presenting challenges for both newcomers and young Canadians entering the workforce. 7 per cent) of recent working-age immigrants experienced difficulties finding their first job in Canada. 3 per cent said they lacked connections in the Canadian job market. 6 per cent said employers did not accept their work experience from outside the country. The figures highlight some of the obstacles facing newcomers, including people who arrive with professional qualifications and years of experience but find it difficult to translate those credentials into employment in Canada. At the same time, competition for entry-level jobs has become a concern for younger Canadians. The Bank of Canada noted in a May 2026 analysis that the influx of young people from abroad between 2022 and 2024 intensified competition for lower-skilled and entry-level positions. It also pointed to economic conditions, changing employer needs and the growing influence of artificial intelligence as other factors affecting young job seekers. Against that backdrop, helping newcomers find employment that makes use of their skills and qualifications remains an important part of their integration into Canadian communities and the broader economy.

Mississauga’s loose leaf vacuum and pickup program is underway. Mississauga’s annual leaf pickup is underway and an interactive city map shows when you can expect crews to arrive in your neighbourhood. The city has revised its leaf vacuum zones from previous years, which means residents should expect changes to their usual pickup collection windows. The city only provides leaf pickup in areas where trees are more than 35 years old and feature a high concentration of large and mature trees. Collection began in late October and is running until early December, divided into three colour zones. Each zone gets two rounds of pickups.

items.title: How can Mississauga residents share feedback on downtown signs and two Cooksville art projects?
items.summary: Mississauga is accepting public feedback on a new downtown wayfinding strategy starting Nov. 21, and artist applications for two Cooksville park installations with deadlines of Nov. 12 and Nov. 23. Mississauga is inviting residents to help shape its downtown look — and calling on artists to bring two Cooksville parks to life. The projects include two permanent art installations and one wayfinding strategy. Mississauga is developing a wayfinding strategy for the downtown area to help residents and visitors navigate safely and explore local businesses, access transit and visit cultural attractions. Starting Nov. 21, the city is inviting residents to submit their feedback via an online survey on the proposed designs that could become permanent signs for wayfinding in downtown. Final designs and an implementation plan will be developed in early 2027, and once funding is secured, signs are expected to be installed starting in April 2027. In the interim, temporary wayfinding signs are posted on windows, walls and sidewalks. The city’s Public Art Program is looking for professional artists or artist-led teams for two Cooksville projects.

items.title: $61-Million Overhaul Puts South Common Community Centre on Track for Spring 2027 Reopening
items.summary: South Common Community Centre and Library in west Mississauga has been closed since June 2024 for a $61-million redevelopment, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that the facility, which first opened in 1981, is expected to reopen to the public in spring 2027 after nearly three years of work. City officials said the project will add an expanded fitness space and a new aquatics centre, along with a larger library and a parkland link connecting the site to South Common Park. Before the reopening, the City of Mississauga plans to survey community members this coming January to help decide which programs the revamped centre should offer, insauga.com said. A virtual information session covering the proposed programs is scheduled for February, according to the report. Renderings released by the city show plans for a new play area and splash pad as part of the redevelopment, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Ontario Reappoints Longtime Mississauga Politician Nando Iannicca to Head Peel Region
items.summary: The Ontario government has appointed Nando Iannicca to continue serving as Peel Region's chair, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that the province named Iannicca as one of eight regional and county heads it appointed across Ontario for the upcoming council term on Tuesday. Unlike in previous terms, insauga.com noted, his selection came through this new provincial appointment process rather than a vote by Regional Council. Iannicca has deep roots in local politics, having represented Mississauga's Ward 7, where he was born and raised, for roughly 30 years after his first election in 1988. During that time, the outlet said, he sat on bodies including the Peel Police Services Board, Credit Valley Conservation and the Mississauga Hospital Foundation board. Regional Council first appointed him chair in 2022, and insauga.com reported that his latest appointment extends his leadership of Peel Region, which covers Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, into the 2026-2030 term beginning Nov. 15.

items.title: Multiple Roads Shut Near Creditview and Sherwood Mills After Driver Strikes Pedestrian
items.summary: Peel Regional Police shut down several roads near Creditview Road on Tuesday morning after a vehicle struck a pedestrian in Mississauga, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that a female pedestrian suffered serious injuries in the collision and was taken by paramedics to a local trauma centre. Police did not release further details about the woman's condition or identity, insauga.com said. The driver involved stayed at the scene following the crash, according to the report. To manage the aftermath, police closed southbound Creditview Road at Willowvale Garden, eastbound Princelea Place toward Creditview Road, and westbound Sherwood Mills Boulevard at Brockworth Drive. Insauga.com noted that officers asked drivers in the area to expect delays and seek alternate routes while the roads remained shut.

items.title: October Sales Data Puts Mississauga's Average Home Price Just Above $927,000
items.summary: Mississauga's average home price slipped 0.2 per cent to $927,521 in October 2026, according to the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board. The board's latest figures showed 508 total home sales in the city last month, with properties sitting on the market for an average of 35 days and 2,342 active listings remaining at month's end. Detached houses accounted for 200 of those sales, averaging 32 days on the market, with 894 such listings still active when October closed. Semi-detached homes saw 67 sales and an average of 29 days on the market, leaving 204 active listings. Attached houses were the slowest-moving segment, with just 17 sales and an average of 30 days on the market against 63 active listings. Townhouse-style condos recorded 94 sales over an average of 35 days on the market, with 356 listings still active at month's end, the board's figures showed.
